Instead of matching exact words, the system understands semantic similarity.
Example:

authentication
token verification
login validation
auth middleware
are related concepts.

24. Important Concepts
4.1 What Is Semantic Search?
Traditional search:
authentication == authentication
Semantic search:

Does this text MEAN something similar?
Example:
Query Matching Code
login verification verify_token()
user auth validate_jwt()
payment processingprocess_transaction()
The AI understands meaning instead of exact words.
4.2 What Are Embeddings?
Embeddings are numerical representations of meaning.
Example:
"authentication"
→ [0.22, -0.44, 0.91, ...]
"verify token"
→ [0.20, -0.41, 0.89, ...]
These vectors become mathematically close because the meanings are related.
34.3 Why Vectors?
AI models canno

t directly understand raw text.
So text is converted into:
numbers → vectors → embeddings
Then mathematics is used to compare meanings.
4.4 What Is Cosine Similarity?
Cosine similarity measures:
How similar are two vectors?
Values:
Value Meaning
1 Very similar
0 Unrelated
-1 Opposite
Visualization:
authentication  ↗
verify token    ↗
similar direction
→ high similarity
4.5 What Is a Vector Database?
A vector database stores embeddings and performs similarity search.
Instead of:
4Find exact words

it does:
Find nearest vectors
Popular vector databases:
Tool Type
FAISS Local vector search
ChromaDBBeginner-friendly vector DB
Pinecone Cloud vector DB
Weaviate Production vector DB
For beginners:
Start with FAISS
4.6 What Is Chunking?
Large files are difficult for AI systems.
Instead of embedding entire files:
# BAD
whole_file_embedding
we split code into smaller pieces.
Example chunks:
deflogin_user():
defverify_token():
5These smaller units are called:
chunks
4.7 Why Chunking Matters
Good c

hunking improves:
search accuracy
retrieval quality
AI explanations
context relevance
Poor chunking leads to:
irrelevant results
noisy retrieval
weak AI answers
Chunking is one of the most important parts of RAG systems.
4.8 What Is RAG?
RAG = Retrieval Augmented Generation
Pipeline:
User Question
      ↓
Retrieve Relevant Chunks
      ↓
Send Chunks to LLM
      ↓
Generate Answer

ions 2. sends them to LLM 3. LLM explains the flow
This is how many AI assistants work.
4.9 What Is AST?
AST = Abstract Syntax Tree
It converts code into structured representations.
Example:
deflogin():
becomes:
Function Definition
instead of plain text.
4.10 Why AST Matters
Without AST:
Chunk = random lines
With AST:
Chunk = actual function/class
This dramatically improves semantic retrieval.

Phase 1 — Learn Embeddings

Understanding This Code
SentenceTransformer
Loads a pretrained embedding model.
all-MiniLM-L6-v2
A lightweight embedding model.
It converts text into vectors.
encode()
Converts text into embeddings.
Step 3 — Build Tiny Semantic Search
fromsentence_transformersimportSentenceTransformer
fromsklearn.metrics.pairwiseimportcosine_similarity
model= SentenceTransformer('all-MiniLM-L6-v2')
documents= [
"user authentication system",
"payment gateway integration",

se connection logic",

]
embeddings= model.encode(documents)
query= "login validation"
query_embedding= model.encode([query])
scores= cosine_similarity(query_embedding, embeddings)
best_index= scores.argmax()
print(documents[best_index])
